video_title: ‘IT DRIVES ME CRAZY’ 😳 Chuck on the perception of OKC’s ‘physical’ defense on Wemby | Inside the NBA

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC's physical strategy to wear down Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: They are throwing bodies at him, they are trying to wear him down, they are trying to make him play in crowds.
quotes.quote: They are throwing bodies at him, they are trying to wear him down, they are trying to make him play in crowds. They are being as physical as possible with him, but you mentioned the monster Game 1 that he had. He played 49 minutes. That is the most of his career and he finished that game strong. But we are talking about a series that is every other day and OKC just has such a deep team. You see the depth with how lopsided the bench scoring is. They just scored 76 bench points, but you also feel that depth defensively, especially Victor Wembanyama. He is dealing with Isaiah Hartenstein and it is Chet Holmgren. Then coming off the bench, there is an Alex Caruso. There is a Jalen Williams, when the other Jalen Williams is healthy, he will take a turn on them. As Chet Holmgren said, the fresh legs out there really are able to try to wear him down, but they are not putting fresh legs on floor just to wear him down. As Chet so eloquently said, the dudes that are going in the game are dudes. OKC goes a legit 12 or 13 deep and a lot of these guys are coming into the game like the scoring is almost a bonus. These are physical, tough players and they are really making Wemby fight for every inch on the floor. Six dunks in Game 1, a total of two in Games 2 and 3.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC's bench thrives on Spurs' defensive strategy against Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.excerpt: These are Spurs game plan designed like, 'Hey, we want those guys shooting those shots because we don't want Shai Gilgeous-Alexander to be able to get where he wants to go.'
quotes.quote: A lot of these three-pointers, these are Spurs game plan designed like, 'Hey, we want those guys shooting those shots because we don't want Shai Gilgeous-Alexander to be able to get where he wants to go.' They are trying to, they are really crowding things, they are clogging the driving lanes against Shai and they are invitation threes, or at least they were. Alex Caruso, 5 of 21 during the regular season on threes against the Spurs. The game plan worked. He was 2 of 12 on Christmas. He is lights out in this series, but he is the epitome of a playoff riser. He shot better than 40% from three in last year's playoff run, which obviously ended in a championship for the Thunder. They have got shooters. Isaiah Joe is barely playing this series. He is a shooter. Jared McCain, I am not so sure that Daryl Morey sold high after all. He just has zero fear, right? But he comes in and his teammates say, 'You know what is going up,' and you always feel like it is going in when the ball hits his hands. Again, it is just they have got all these guys who know their roles, they play with confidence, they play with freedom and they are taking the shots that are presented to them because the Spurs don't want to let the two-time MVP dominate the game.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs' strategy to get Shai Gilgeous-Alexander off the ball
quotes.excerpt: Make him play in crowds, get him off the ball. To sum it up briefly, it is get him off the ball.
quotes.quote: Make him play in crowds, get him off the ball. To sum it up briefly, it is get him off the ball. Steph Castle is taking the primary assignment. They are giving him a lot of help, which he is usually not a guy who gets a lot of help. That is the kind of weapon that Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is. They are doubling often, they are doubling randomly, so it is not predictable for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. They are basically daring him, make quote-unquote the right play, make the right read, get off the ball, don't try to force anything. It hasn't been the biggest scoring series for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, just like by the way it wasn't last series against the Lakers, but he is making the right plays, he is getting his teammates open shots and he has had 12 assists in two of these games during the series. That is a playoff career high. So that just proves that he is reading the game and he is if you don't want to let him dominate, he is going to trust his teammates and his teammates delivered last series, they are delivering again right now.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs face immense pressure and injury challenges in Game 4
quotes.excerpt: This is a huge test. This is the biggest test of Victor Wembanyama's career.
quotes.quote: This is a huge test. This is the biggest test of Victor Wembanyama's career. The Spurs came into this series with a ton of confidence. They beat the Thunder four out of five times during the regular season. That included three wins in 12 days after the Thunder got off to that 24 and 1 start. They spanked their butts in front of a national TV audience on Christmas Day in OKC's gym, but the playoffs are a different beast. Let's just also call it like it is for the Spurs. This is not a healthy Spurs team. They have a blank injury report right now, but De'Aaron Fox is clearly not 100%. He is playing through a high ankle sprain. Dillon Harper is playing through adductor soreness. He is clearly not 100%. As Mr. Johnson said today, Victor Wembanyama creates a lot of the advantages and then those Spurs guards throughout the course of the year have been great at exploiting them. That hasn't really happened in this series. Fox missed the first couple games, Harper wasn't the same player in Game 3, but there are no excuses. There is pressure and for a team that is trying to skip the line, trying to win a championship in their first playoffs together, I agree with you. You can't let this thing go back to OKC down 3-1.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green highlights OKC's deep and talented bench
quotes.excerpt: All those guys on that bench, they all can play. And you have Jalen Duren out.
quotes.quote: It is unbelievable, but it just shows you really how deep this team is. They have built this from the ground up. So all those guys on that bench, they all can play. And you have Jalen Duren out. So all of those guys when they are coming in, Jared McCain last night I think shot 23 shots, or 21 shots. All those guys that are coming in, they have more of a green light to just go because Jalen Duren's not out there. AJ Mitchell got hurt last night, he left the game. So all those guys have an opportunity to just go, but also if you look at that, maybe not Jalen Williams, but three of those four guys could be starters on other teams in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Charles Barkley
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley slams Spurs' 'trash' game plan and 'soft' fouls
quotes.excerpt: The Spurs' game plan is trash, terrible. Because them guys getting wide open shots like they're taking the ball out of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's hand.
quotes.quote: But two things. The Spurs' game plan is trash, terrible. Because them guys getting wide open shots like they're taking the ball out of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's hand. They're just getting jump shot practices. So their game plan is helping them. They're doubling Shai so far away, these guys just sitting over there like they're in the gym by themselves. And the second thing is, I think we need to all pray for Wemby. Because he can't play too many minutes, they're going to kill him out there. Man, I am damn sure joking. Because you guys, these people, man, they're pissing me off. I'm watching the whole games. They ain't playing dirty. These are some of the softest fouls I ever seen in my life. You got these clowns on TV talking about, 'Oh, they're going to hurt poor Wemby.' I was like, 'Hurt him? Are you kidding me, man?' It drives me crazy watching these shows.

quotes.speaker: Shaquille O'Neal
quotes.summary_phrase: Shaquille O'Neal demands more dominance from Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to need Victor Wembanyama to do more. Game 1 he had 41, 24, they won. Game 2, 21, 26, it's not enough.
quotes.quote: That's how they win games. You focus on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, 'Oh my God, it's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, two-time MVP.' And like Chuck said, they're wide open shots. And I'm going to need Victor Wembanyama to do more. Game 1 he had 41, 24, they won. Game 2, 21, 26, it's not enough. And I can say that as the Lord Supreme of all big men. I remember getting swept averaging 34, 35, and my father, rest in peace him, 'It ain't enough, you have to do more.' So he has to do more. I heard him yesterday say he's not making his teammates better, it's because he's not dominating the game. When Alex Caruso is on you, I don't want to see a turnaround. I do not want to see a turnaround. He has to be aggressive, super aggressive, so they can panic with him and free up the other guys.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Smith praises OKC's 'special others' for their scoring depth
quotes.excerpt: They have 11 guys on their team I would believe that if you got they got 20 points, no one would be surprised.

text_blocks.speaker: Kenny Smith
text_blocks.text: No, but you have a term called others. I'm going to elevate it a little bit. I'm going to call them special others. Because they have 11 guys on their team I would believe that if you got they got 20 points, no one would be surprised. If you say Isaiah Joe gets 20 points, no one would be surprised.

text_blocks.speaker: Charles Barkley
text_blocks.text: Yeah, okay, he's done that. But the Spurs are helping them with that bad game plan.

text_blocks.speaker: Kenny Smith
text_blocks.text: No, I'm not saying that anybody can make wide open shots. No, but I'm saying that these guys have done it when when Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has gone out and they still had it rolling. You had multiple guys when they had to take multiple shots, from Caruso to Wiggins to Wallace to McCain. These guys are not unaccustomed to getting 20 points either. So they're helping them, but these guys are special others. They're not just like he said, three or four of them could start on most teams.
